description.narrative:
South African Institute for International Affairs (SAIIA) är en icke-statlig researchfokuserad tankesmedja som grundades 1934 med uppdraget att uppmuntra bredare och informerad medvetenhet, debatt och analys om internationella angelägenheter. Dess övergripande mål är att bidra till "ett välstyrt, fredligt, ekonomiskt hållbart och globalt engagerat Afrika".
För att uppnå detta bedriver institutet evidensbaserad policyforskning och engagerar nationella, regionala och internationella beslutsfattare i policyutformning. Institutet bygger också kapacitet hos nationella, regionala, kontinentala och icke-statliga aktörer för att de ska kunna engagera sig med respektive regeringar och afrikanska styrelseinstitutioner.
SAIIA har varit en Sida-partner sedan 2005. Sida fortsatte sitt samarbete med SAIIA genom att ge kärnstöd under strategiperioden 2016-2021. Det senaste kärnavtalet löper ut i december 2021. SAIIA har ansökt om fortsatt kärnstöd om totalt 37 miljoner kronor för att under perioden 2021-2025 genomföra sin verksamhet. Det ansökta årliga beloppet är 9.25 miljoner kronor. SAIIAs föreslagna program ligger väl i linje med Sveriges strategi för regionalt utvecklingssamarbete med Afrika söder om Sahara. Bidraget till denna insats bedöms strategiskt då det stärker pågående arbete med forskning på frågor som är aktuella förr den afrikanska kontinenten med syfte att informera och påverka beslutsfattare och på sikt bidra till ett Afrika präglat av god samhällsstyrning, fred och ekonomisk hållbarhet. Initiativet uppfyller Sidas bedömningskriterier.

The South African Institute for International Affairs (SAIIA) is a nongovernmental research-focused think tank established in 1934 with the mandate to encourage wider and informed awareness, debate and analysis on international affairs. Its overarching goal is to contribute to “a well-governed, peaceful, economically sustainable and globally engaged Africa”. To achieve this, the Institute conducts evidence-based policy research and engages national, regional and international policymakers on policy formulation. It also builds capacity of national, regional, continental and non-state actors to engage with respective governments and African governance institutions. Sida has since 2005 been a partner to the SAIIA. Sida continued its collaboration with SAIIA by providing core support during the strategy period 2016-2021. The most recent core agreement will come to an end in December 2021.
The overall goal of SAIIA is to contribute towards a well-governed, peaceful, economically sustainable and globally engaged Africa. Under this overall goal are four key result areas (KRA), each with their own expected outcomes, as follows: KRA 1. Contribute to strengthening governance, stability and accountability in Africa within the framework of key African and global governance mechanisms and initiatives with a specific focus on the APRM. KRA 2. Contribute towards enhanced climate change resilience and green economic development in Africa in a manner that enables a just transition. KRA 3. Contribute to sustainable and inclusive economic growth and resilience in Africa by pursuing greater economic integration through processes such as the AfCFTA and harnessing the opportunities offered by the Digital Economy in support of greater social inclusion. KRA 4. Contribute to building more effective African agency on new geopolitical and normative challenges in regional and multilateral fora, including the G20, as well as its external partnerships. The primary target group of SAIIA’s research outputs and engagements are African policymakers at the national, regional and continental levels. Other target groups include policy makers responsible for policymaking with an impact on Africa in international organisations such as the European Union, various UN bodies, the OECD, BRICS, the WTO and the G20. SAIIA also actively engages foreign governments that are involved in Africa such as European states, China, Brazil, the US, Russia and India. Finally, SAIIA targets the African media both as a dissemination channel of its research findings but also to build its capacity in areas within SAIIA's expertise.

description.narrative:
SAIIAs performance over the year reflects an organisation that has delivered and achieved meaningful outcomes across all four thematic areas. Throughout 2025, SAIIA demonstrated its continued relevance and influence in African policy spaces, strengthening its role as a trusted partner to governments, regional bodies, civil society and youth constituencies.
Under Theme 1: African Governance, Democracy and Human Rights in the Digital Age, SAIIA made notable progress in deepening civic participation, particularly among young people and women. The Youth Submission to the African Peer Review Mechanism (APRM) in South Africa stands out as a key achievement. This initiative not only empowered young participants and equipped them with governancerelated skills, but also successfully positioned youth voices within national governance processes. The initiative served as a model for how civil society can meaningfully influence continental governance mechanisms.
Work under Theme 2: Sustainable and Just Climate Transitions continued to elevate SAIIA as a technical leader in climate policy. The organisation contributed directly to the African Unions Climate Change and Resilient Development Strategy and supported regional bodies such as IGAD in strengthening their adaptation frameworks. At national level, SAIIA informed South Africas work on ecosystembased coastal and marine adaptation. These contributions ensured that key regional and continental climate policies were grounded in robust evidence and better aligned with African priorities for resilience and sustainability.
Despite facing staff turnover, Theme 3: African Economic Resilience and Inclusion generated important outputs that influenced policy thinking on vulnerability and economic inclusion. The development of the Social Vulnerability Index and new climateeconomic indices attracted interest from institutions such as UNECA and helped deepen understanding of socioeconomic resilience across the continent. SAIIA also supported the ongoing implementation and monitoring mechanisms of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), contributing analytical tools that strengthened how progress is assessed and reported.
Notable achievements were also from Theme 4: African Agency and International Relations, where SAIIA played a central role in shaping South Africas 2025 G20 Presidency. Its appointment as a colead of the G20 Think 20 (T20) process marked a significant milestone, elevating SAIIAs influence within global governance spaces. The organisations extensive media engagementover 260 appearances, exceeded targetsamplified African perspectives on global issues and strengthened SAIIAs international visibility. Its alignment with South African government departments and African diplomatic communities further reinforced the Institutes credibility as a policy thought leader.
Across all themes, SAIIA maintained its reputation for delivering highquality, evidencebased research while strengthening partnerships and expanding its reach. Challenges remain, particularly around internal capacity, sustainable funding and the need for more consistent crossprogramme collaboration. Yet the progress made this year demonstrates SAIIAs ability to adapt, innovate and lead within an increasingly complex policy environment.
In conclusion, SAIIAs performance over the year reflects a strong and resilient organisation that continues to shape policy conversations at national, regional and global levels. The outcomes achieved across each theme illustrate not only the depth of SAIIAs expertise but also its commitment to advancing a more informed, equitable and sustainable future for Africa.
Key recommendations from the mid-term evaluation include strengthening engagement across the full policy cycle, enhancing collaboration with the private sector, leveraging SAIIAs G20 leadership experience, narrowing the thematic focus to align with internal capacity, clarifying partnership criteria, investing in dedicated proposal-development resources, improving monitoring and evaluation systems, and expanding consultancy services. Overall, SAIIA is assessed as a highly credible and influential African think tank that has delivered substantial value during the 2021-2025 period. Sustained impact will depend on strengthening internal systems, sharpening strategic priorities, and diversifying funding in a sustainable manner.
